name: adaptive-pagination
title: Adaptive pagination
description: One pagination that fits its box: numbered pages when there is room, 'Page 3 of 12' with a list of pages and arrows when there is not.
docs: page is the current page counted from 1 and pageCount how many there are; onPageChange(page) is called with the page asked for. It measures the width of its own container with a ResizeObserver, never the window, so one component fits a narrow card and a wide table footer. When the container is wide enough it shows first, previous, a window of page numbers with ellipses (siblingCount numbers on each side of the current page, 1 by default, always the same number of slots so the row does not jump), next and last. When it is not, it shows previous, a button that reads 'Page 3 of 12' and opens a grid of every page in a dialog named by its heading, 'Go to page' (arrow keys, Home, End and the Page keys move, it opens on the current page), and next. Until it has been measured the compact layout stands in, because it fits anywhere. The current page carries aria-current='page'. The buttons that go back on the first page and the ones that go on at the last are aria-disabled rather than disabled: they keep focus and a tooltip says why ('You are on the first page'). A change of layout never loses the focused control: previous and next are the same elements in both layouts, and a page number, first or last hands focus to the compact label, previous or next (and the label back to the current page number). hrefFor(page) returns an address and turns every control into a real link for crawlers and new tabs; from a Server Component, which cannot pass a function, give hrefTemplate such as '/orders?page={page}'. With a handler too, a plain click goes to onPageChange and a modified click opens the address. The change is announced politely as 'Page 4 of 12'. align places the row (center by default), locale writes the numbers, and labels holds every word for another language.
